hints: Think about where aluminium sits in Period 3 and how bonding changes from left to right across the period.
Remember that $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is a solid with a very high melting point formed between a metal and non-metal, which points to one type of bonding.
Recall what happens when aluminium oxide meets both strong acids and strong alkalis, and what special word describes that dual behaviour.
walkthrough:
**Place aluminium oxide in Period 3**

Think of the Period 3 oxides from $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ to $\text{SiO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$. Bonding changes from ionic on the left to covalent on the right.

Aluminium is on the left side as a metal, so its oxide is mainly ionic: $\text{Al}^{3+}$ and $\text{O}^{2-}$ ions in a giant lattice.

**Decide ionic vs covalent**

$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ has a giant ionic lattice with a very high melting point. It is not a simple molecule and it is not a giant covalent network like $\text{SiO}_2$.

So we can rule out simple covalent and giant covalent, leaving ionic bonding.

**Decide acid / base nature**

Across Period 3, oxides go from basic ($\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$) to amphoteric ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) to acidic ($\text{SiO}_2$, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, $\text{SO}_3$).

$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 6\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaAl(OH)}_4$$

**Combine both descriptions**

Ionic bonding plus reaction with both acids (acting as a base) and alkalis (acting as an acid) means amphoteric.

That combination matches ionic and amphoteric.

options.A: Incorrect. Simple covalent would mean separate small molecules with low melting point, like $\text{CO}_2$. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is a high melting point giant solid, not a simple molecule, though the amphoteric part is correct.
options.B: Incorrect on both counts. Giant covalent describes $\text{SiO}_2$, which is acidic only. Aluminium is a metal forming $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ions, and its oxide reacts with both acids and bases, not bases only.
options.C: Correct. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ has mainly ionic bonding in a giant lattice, and it is amphoteric because it reacts with acids to form aluminium salts and with concentrated alkalis to form aluminates such as $\text{NaAl(OH)}_4$.
options.D: Half right, half wrong. Bonding is correctly ionic, but basic only describes $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{MgO}$. Aluminium oxide also reacts with bases, so it is amphoteric, not basic only.
